text:
alexander: SLO alert fired for hosted-infer.eu-west1 - sudden p99 5xx surge and increased timeouts. customers reporting errors.

katie: seeing it on the grafana dashboard too, ingress gateway 5xx spike started ~09:12UTC. p50/p95 OK, tail only.

sre-oncall: tagging in. any correlation with deploys? ci pipeline shows no recent prod rollouts for gateway.

alexander: no deploys. error types look like upstream connection resets and grpc stream terminations in logs. quick log query I ran: `status>=500 | count() by upstream_service,reason` shows most from infer-proxy-v2 -> hostpool-timeout.

maria: customer-support: two customers reported long tail timeouts when sending batch requests. provided curl repro, I'll paste: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"model":"gpt-os","input":"x"}' -v --max-time 15
```

katie: adding trace sampling note: we have heavy trace sampling turned down for high qps routes, might be why traces are sparse. obs-bot: run trace-coverage check please.

obs-bot: trace-coverage job started for hosted-infer.eu-west1. preliminary: only ~12% of 5xx requests have associated spans due to sampler rules.

alexander: that explains missing context. can someone run kv-cache and batcher metrics for proxy? `sum(rate(kv_cache.evictions[5m]))` looked elevated 09:10-09:14.

sre-oncall: running checks on pool sizes and connection counts. early result: infer-pool-usw2 had surge? wait, wrong region. eu-west1 pool shows abrupt increase in inflight connections to model backends around 09:11. attaching query: `sum(rate(proxy_out.connections_active{region="eu-west1"}[1m])) by (backend)`

katie: also seeing a burst of large requests (long seq len) that bypass small-batch path, causing head-of-line. batcher queue length spiked.

maria: CS asking for timeline and ETA to share with customers. any mitigation steps?

alexander: short-term mitigation: 1) reduce sampling for this route so traces capture failures, 2) temporarily enable fallback model variant with lower token count, 3) increase pool size/burst capacity for eu-west1. any objections?

sre-oncall: will open a capacity bump for eu-west1 and flip fallback canary. doing 2 and 3 now.

katie: I can relax sampler to 100% for error responses only: `trace.sample.rule: if status>=500 => sample_rate=1.0` then re-run trace query.

obs-bot: sampler change applied. new traces should appear within ~30s.

alexander: posting a couple of quick log queries for postmortem: 1) `http_request | where region=="eu-west1" and status>=500 | parse message with *` 2) `latency_ms>5000 and status!=200 | count()`

sre-oncall: capacity bump complete, added +3 backends to eu-west1 pool and enabled fallback route. early telemetry: error fraction falling from 0.85% -> 0.22% in last 2m.

maria: updated customers with "we've applied temporary capacity and fallback; investigating root cause and will follow up". CS requests timeline and if billing credits needed.

katie: we should check whether the batcher batching policy mis-classified some large requests causing poor kernel selection. opening a ticket with eng-runtime.

alexander: agree. recording action items: A) eng-runtime to reproduce large-request head-of-line, B) infra to evaluate autoscale thresholds for eu-west1, C) obs to add alert for trace-coverage drop under 25% when SLO burns happen, D) CS to collate affected customer IDs.

customer-support: collecting affected request ids and customer traces where available. sending to #support-escalations.

obs-bot: SLO alert cleared. p99 5xx down to 0.18% and decreasing. traces increased to ~68% coverage for error paths.

alexander: thanks team. we'll keep monitoring for 2 hours. tagging eng-runtime and infra to follow up in the postmortem.

katie: small note for postmortem: include the curl repro and the exact log lines for the hostpool-timeout reasons.

sre-oncall: closing the oncall handoff. if it recurs, please re-open thread and escalate to pager. :white_check_mark:
